newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds firm, MCI flat, offers pulled.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds firm, MCI flat, offers pulled.

text.p: Fresh U.S. corporate bond paper traded at or near issue bid at midday signifying a strong underlying bid as interest rates tick lower, dealers said.
Spreads for MCI Communications debt were unchanged as its equity posted marginal gains, meanwhile.

MCI debt firmed seven basis points on Friday after British Telecommunications Plc confirmed it would consider a proposal to the 80 percent of the company it does not already own, traders said. BT on Sunday confirmed its plans to merge with MCI in a deal worth more than $20 billion.
Offers to sell MCI and BT paper vanished, a trader said.
Standard & Poor's and Fitch Investors Service on Monday said they may raise their ratings on MCI debt in light of the proposed merger. Moody's affirmed its ratings on MCI.
At the same time, S&P and Moody's said they may downgrade their ratings of BT debt.

More active on Monday was J.C. Penney debt after the retailer's $3.3 billion cash, stock and debt offer for Eckerd Corp, according to traders. The debt widened by 10 basis points across the curve, said one trader at a New York shop.
J.C. Penney 7.05s of 2005 were 10 basis points wider at 70 bid, 65 offer, the trader said.

Elsewhere, dealers said anticipation over the U.S. elections on Tuesday overshadowed and exacerbated typically dull Monday trade. Prices were little changed and the tone remained substantive after the market absorbed more the more than $6.0 billion new supply of last week, dealers added.

"There's still very good sponsorship in the corporate market, and for that matter all the markets," said a head of taxable fixed-income at a regional firm. "All the spreads are tight and people are buying on dips."
Prices were flat to up with Treasuries, which marked thin ranges afore elections and refunding auctions, analysts said.

Reflecting firm market tone, Tribune Co's $250 million 6-7/8 percent debt and May Department Stores $125 million 6-7/8 percent debt were quoted at issued spreads of 54 and 51 basis points over the Treasury curve, respectively.
Turning to high-yielders, traders said the BT/MCI proposed merger ignited trade for telecommunication debt.

Robert Waldman, head of corporate bond research at Salomon Brothers, said MCI indicated in its conference call that BT's expertise will allow it to continue to push into the $100 billion local U.S. telephone loop.
